title: Bundle Economics and Self-Serve to Enterprise Bridges
description: Master advanced bundling economics, cannibalization analysis, and designing self-serve to enterprise conversion paths.

interactions.prompt: Which metric best reveals whether your bundle is destroying value rather than creating it?

options.text: Bundle attach rate exceeding 60% of new deals
Negative incremental revenue per bundle vs à la carte mix
High NPS scores among bundle purchasers
Bundle SKU becoming the top-selling package

interactions.teachingPreamble: Bundle cannibalization occurs when customers who would have paid more à la carte switch to a discounted bundle, destroying margin. Microsoft found that early Office 365 bundles cannibalized higher-margin standalone Exchange and SharePoint deals before rebalancing tier composition. The key diagnostic is measuring whether incremental revenue per customer is positive or negative versus the counterfactual product mix.

interactions.prompt: A B2B SaaS company launched a 3-product bundle at 25% discount. Pre-bundle ARPU: $142. Post-bundle ARPU: $131. New customer acquisition rose 18%. Existing customer bundle adoption: 41%. What's the critical signal?

options.text: New customer growth justifies the ARPU decline
41% existing adoption signals heavy cannibalization outweighing acquisition gains
The 25% discount is standard and acceptable
ARPU will recover naturally as customers expand usage

interactions.prompt: When designing a self-serve to enterprise bridge, what is the most effective structural mechanism?

options.text: Hard paywalling all collaboration features behind enterprise tier
Usage-based triggers that create natural friction points requiring sales contact
Offering enterprise discounts to any customer who requests them
Removing the self-serve tier entirely after 12 months

interactions.teachingPreamble: Slack's self-serve to enterprise bridge is a masterclass: teams grow organically on free/pro tiers, but governance needs (SSO, compliance, cross-workspace discovery) create natural friction as organizations scale past ~200 users. Datadog similarly uses usage-based metering where infrastructure monitoring costs scale predictably until a threshold triggers enterprise negotiation. The best bridges feel like natural progressions, not artificial walls.

interactions.prompt: In bundle pricing theory, the 'reservation price ____' effect explains why bundling works: customers' willingness-to-pay for individual products varies, but bundled WTP has lower variance, enabling higher average capture.

options.text: averaging
anchoring
maximizing
stacking

interactions.prompt: Your PLG SaaS has 12,000 self-serve accounts. Enterprise sales wants to gate SSO and audit logs behind a $50K/yr enterprise tier. Product argues this punishes security-conscious SMBs and increases churn. Which path do you take?

options.text: Gate SSO/audit fully behind enterprise—it's the strongest conversion lever
Include basic SSO in mid-tier; gate advanced compliance and admin controls
Make SSO free for all tiers to maximize adoption and reduce churn
Offer SSO as a standalone $5K/yr add-on across all tiers

interactions.prompt: A company with 3 tiers sees 72% of revenue from the middle tier. What is the most strategically concerning implication?

options.text: The top tier lacks differentiated value; enterprise upsell path is broken
The bottom tier is priced too low and should be eliminated
Middle tier concentration is ideal and indicates strong product-market fit
The company should add a fourth tier between middle and top

interactions.teachingPreamble: Healthy tier distributions typically follow a pattern where 10-20% of revenue comes from the entry tier (acquisition), 40-50% from mid-tier (core), and 30-40% from the top tier (expansion). When HubSpot noticed over-concentration in their Professional tier, they redesigned Enterprise with exclusive features like custom objects and sandboxes—shifting 15% of revenue upward within two quarters. Extreme mid-tier concentration signals a broken upsell narrative.

interactions.prompt: Your analytics platform is redesigning its packaging. Rank these initiatives by expected revenue impact for a company with strong PLG motion and 800 enterprise prospects in pipeline: (a) Restructure bundles to reduce cannibalization, (b) Build usage-based enterprise conversion triggers, (c) Add a new premium add-on for advanced AI features, (d) Simplify self-serve tier from 4 tiers to 2.

options.text: Restructure bundles to reduce cannibalization
Build usage-based enterprise conversion triggers
Add premium AI feature add-on
Simplify self-serve from 4 tiers to 2

interactions.prompt: Your largest competitor just made their equivalent of your gated enterprise features completely free. Enterprise pipeline conversion drops 30% in two weeks. How do you respond?

options.text: Match competitor—ungating enterprise features and competing on service and support
Shift enterprise value prop to outcomes: dedicated CSM, SLAs, custom integrations
Aggressively discount enterprise tier by 40% to win back pipeline
Acquire a complementary product to create a differentiated bundle competitor can't match

interactions.priorContext: Previously you designed usage-based enterprise conversion triggers and gated advanced compliance features behind your enterprise tier. Now a competitor has made equivalent features free, undermining your gating strategy.
